page.title: Choosing a Webinar Production Company
page.description: Learn what services, timelines, costs and tools to evaluate before hiring a webinar production partner for virtual or hybrid events.
page.h1: What should you decide first about a webinar production company?
page.definition: A webinar production company is a service provider that plans, runs and records live online events on the platform you choose, handling run of show, speaker rehearsals, branded graphics, live moderation, a backup stream and post‑event editing.
page.quick_answer: Start by choosing the platform you will stream on and confirm who owns the run of show; then request a scoped quote. West Peek Productions produces virtual, hybrid and webinar events and sets up marketing, content and creative operations.

sections.h2: What services should a webinar production company cover?

blocks.p: A production company should handle the run of show, speaker rehearsals, branded graphics, live moderation, a backup stream and post‑event editing. The deliverables typically include a detailed run of show, speaker brief and rehearsal, branded slide template and lower thirds, live producer, Q&A moderation, backup stream, edited recording and clips.

ul: Run of show and speaker brief
Branded slide template and lower thirds

sections.h2: How long does it take to produce a webinar versus a summit?

blocks.p: A standard webinar needs three to four weeks from brief to live, while a summit or online conference requires six to eight weeks. The timeline follows seven stages, each with one owner and one output.

sections.h2: What are the typical cost models for webinar production?

blocks.p: Three cost models dominate: per‑host licences tied to attendee capacity, self‑serve monthly plans, and annual contracts negotiated by sales. Moderated webinars generally fall in the $2,500 to $7,500 range, while executive summits and hybrid productions start at $10,000 to $50,000 and above.

sections.h2: Which tools do production teams use for planning and execution?

blocks.p: Teams rely on project boards, document editors, publishing platforms and analytics suites to keep every workstream on track. Common choices include Asana, Monday.com or Airtable for the calendar; Google Docs or Notion for briefs; WordPress, Webflow or HubSpot for publishing; GA4 and HubSpot for reporting.

sections.h2: What should you decide before hiring a production partner?

blocks.p: Lock the event platform, define ownership of the run of show, set rehearsal dates and agree on replay delivery before signing a contract. Clear decisions on these points prevent scope creep and missed deadlines.

ul: Schedule full rehearsal two to five days before live
Confirm replay delivery within 24 to 48 hours

faq.q: Do I need a separate platform licence if I hire a production company?
faq.a: Yes. The platform is software you licence; production is the crew, cameras, encoder, run of show and backup stream. You purchase both, though the production partner can help you select the right platform.

faq.q: How many people are needed to run a simple webinar?
faq.a: One producer can run a simple webinar. Summits and hybrid events need a show caller, speaker manager, moderator and platform operator.

faq.q: When should the replay be sent to attendees?
faq.a: Send the replay within 24 to 48 hours while attendees still remember the event. This timing maximises engagement and lead capture.

faq.q: What is the typical lead time for a hybrid conference?
faq.a: Plan a hybrid conference six to eight weeks out; lock the venue AV and the platform before the agenda is final.
